action: USMH advises affected customers to beware of emails posing as the company and says it never asks for passwords, codes or card numbers by email or phone; do not open unexpected links or attachments.
date_note: USMH's notice is dated 12 November; it gives no date for the access itself. Security NEXT was published on 20 November.
exec: Unauthorized access to a retailer's shopping app system may have exposed names and email addresses of 64,003 accounts.
plain: Hackers got into the system behind a Japanese supermarket group's shopping app; names and email addresses of 64,003 accounts may have leaked, though the company has not confirmed they were taken.

sources.name: NHK (lead paragraph only; article body gated)

summary: United Super Markets Holdings (USMH) said on 12 November that a third party gained unauthorized access to the system of its Scan&Go ignica shopping app. A file on that system held names and email addresses entered at registration for 64,003 of about 2.4 million app accounts. USMH says it has not confirmed that the data was actually taken, and no misuse or secondary harm has been confirmed.
title: USMH: unauthorized access to Scan&Go ignica app system, 64,003 accounts' names and emails may have leaked

validation.note: USMH's own notice (PDF, 12 Nov) read in full by the follow-up desk; Security NEXT and NHK report the same figures. The notice gives no cause, access date or attacker.

review.note: Re-review: title, 12 Nov date, 64,003 of about 2.4 million accounts, names and emails, leak not confirmed, no misuse, action advice against USMH PDF; Security NEXT (20 Nov) agrees.
